story.eli5: Tiny Shop is a cricket stadium where fans buy things. Fans look at the stalls, pick items, and pay at the ticket counter. Most of the stadium is built. But the ticket counter can be tricked, anyone can knock down a stall, and the refund window is an empty room.
story.teammate: Tiny Shop is a small online shop backend: the stalls (products API), the scorer's desk (orders API) and the ticket counter (Stripe payments). The happy path works: list products, place an order, start a Stripe payment. The weak spots: the Stripe webhook trusts anyone, the price comes from the customer, product deletion has no login check, and refunds are an empty function.
story.senior: Express 4 + Mongoose API with three routers (/products, /orders, /payments) and JWT auth middleware. Stripe PaymentIntents are created with a client-supplied amount; the webhook marks orders paid without signature verification; DELETE /products/:id is unauthenticated; /payments/refund is an empty async handler that never responds. No tests, no input validation, secrets hardcoded in two places.

explain.eli5: Fans walk in through three gates: the stalls, the scorer's desk and the ticket counter. Every gate writes into the same scorebook. The ticket counter talks to the bank, and the bank radios back when money arrives. The announcer shouts out receipts.
explain.teammate: src/server.js opens the stadium: it mounts three routers (/products, /orders, /payments) and connects to MongoDB (the scorebook). Orders and payments sit behind the gate security (requireAuth). Payments talk to Stripe (the bank), and Stripe calls back through the webhook radio. Orders ask the announcer (Nodemailer) to send a receipt.
explain.senior: Single Express process. server.js mounts routers at /products, /orders and /payments, enables cors() with defaults and express.json(), then connects Mongoose with MONGO_URL before listen(). requireAuth (JWT, hardcoded secret) guards orders and checkout/refund but not product deletion or the webhook. External dependencies: Stripe (PaymentIntents + webhook), SMTP via Nodemailer.

explain.teammate: POST /orders (login required) creates an order with the items and amount from the request, lowers stock for each product one at a time, and fires a receipt email. GET /orders/mine lists your own orders.

findings.title: Stripe webhook does not verify the signature

explain.eli5: When the bank radios 'paid!', the scorer writes 'paid' without checking it's really the bank. Anyone can pretend.
explain.teammate: The webhook reads req.body and marks the order paid. It never checks Stripe's signature header, so anyone who knows the URL can mark any order as paid.
explain.senior: No stripe.webhooks.constructEvent(rawBody, sig, secret). express.json() runs globally, so the raw body needed for verification isn't even available on this route.

why_it_matters.eli5: People can get things for free.
why_it_matters.teammate: Free orders for anyone who sends a fake request.
why_it_matters.senior: Direct revenue loss; order state can be forged.

fix.eli5: Check the bank's secret stamp on every radio call.
fix.teammate: Use Stripe's webhook signing secret to verify each event.
fix.senior: Mount the webhook with express.raw({type:'application/json'}) before express.json(), verify with stripe.webhooks.constructEvent(req.body, req.headers['stripe-signature'], process.env.STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET), and make the handler idempotent.

findings.title_eli5: Shelves are counted one item at a time, and can go below zero
findings.title: Stock update is N+1, non-atomic, and unchecked

explain.eli5: For each item, the scorer walks to the shelf, takes one off, and walks back. Two fans at once can grab the last snack, and the shelf can say -1.
explain.teammate: Stock is lowered in a loop with one database trip per item, with no check that enough stock exists, and no protection when two orders happen at the same time.
explain.senior: findById + save per item: N+1 round trips, a read-modify-write race, no stock >= qty guard, and a TypeError if a productId is unknown (product is null). The order is created before stock is checked.

why_it_matters.eli5: You can sell snacks you don't have.

why_it_matters.senior: Data integrity + latency; crashes on bad ids.

fix.eli5: Check the shelf first, and change it in one go.
fix.teammate: Use one atomic update per item that only succeeds if there's enough stock.
fix.senior: Product.updateOne({ _id, stock: { $gte: qty } }, { $inc: { stock: -qty } }) or bulkWrite inside a transaction; validate the items before creating the order.
